docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: The only [[TODO|grammatical category]] exhibited by [[TODO|adverbs]] in [[./index|Modern Greek]] is [[TODO|degree]].

docs.title: Positive Degree
docs.text:
The positive [[Adverbs#Degrees|degree]] of many [[Adverbs|adverbs]] is formed from the [[Adjectives#Positive Degree|positive degree]] of a corresponding [[Adjectives|adjective]].

Most [[Adjectives|adjectives]] in -ος, -η / -α, -ο, in -ύς, -ιά, -ύ and in -ης, -α, -ικο have a corresponding [[Adverbs|adverb]], which is equivalent to their [[TODO|neuter]] [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] and thus ends in -α.

Example: Adverbs in -α

αλύπητος, -η, -ο ("merciless") - αλύπητα ("mercilessly")

τελευταίος, -α, -ο ("recent") - τελευταία ("recently")

βαθύς, -ιά, -ύ ("deep") - βαθιά ("deeply")

Some [[Adjectives|adjectives]] in -ος, -η / -α, -ο have an alternative [[Adverbs|adverb]] formed by adding the suffix -ως to their stem. Such [[Adverbs|adverbs]] derived from [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] [[Adjectives|adjectives]] become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]]. In some situations, there is no difference in meaning between the two variants, but in many others this difference is significant.

Example: Adverbs in -ως from Adjectives in -ος, -η / -α, -ο

ευχάριστος, -η, -ο ("pleasant") - ευχαρίστως ("gladly", "with pleasure"); ευχάριστα ("pleasantly")

τέλειος, -α, -ο ("perfect", "complete") - τελείως ("completely"); τέλεια ("perfectly")

[[Adverbs|Adverbs]] are formed from [[Adjectives|adjectives]] in -ης, -ες by adding the suffix -ως to the their stem. The [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] remains on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] as in the [[TODO|masculine]] [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]]. However, the [[Adverbs|adverbs]] formed from [[Adjectives|adjectives]] in -ώδης are [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]].

Example: Adverbs from Adjectives in -ης, -ες

ακριβής, -ές ("exact") - ακριβώς ("exactly")

ουσιώδης, -ες ("essential") - ουσιωδώς ("essentially")

[[Adverbs|Adverbs]] are formed from [[Adjectives|adjectives]] in -ύς, -εία, -ύ by adding the suffix -έως but are formal and rarely occur in spoken language.

Example: Adverbs from Adjectives in -ύς, -εία, -ύ

βραδύς, -εία, -ύ ("slow") - βραδέως ("slowly")

docs.title: Definiteness
docs.text: [[./index|Modern Greek]] has

docs.title: The Definite Article
docs.text: Similar to how English use the definite article "the", modern Greek has a way to distinguish nouns based on their definiteness.

docs.title: Declension
docs.text:
English has a single definite article, namely the word "the". However, the definite article in modern Greek has multiple forms depending on the gender, case and number of the noun in pertains to.

Singular Plural Masculine Feminine Neuter Masculine Feminine Neuter Nominative ο η το οι τα Genitive του της του των Accusative το(ν) τη(ν) το τους τις τα

The accusative masculine and feminine singular of the [[Articles|definite article]] always end in -ν when the next word starts with a vowel or one of κ, π, τ, ξ, ψ, γκ, μπ, ντ. The final -ν is optional in all other situations. Nevertheless, the full form τον is usually used when the article relates to a proper name such as τον Στέφανο.

docs.title: Declension
docs.text:
These are the forms of the indefinite article of modern Greek.

The Indefinite Article of Modern Greek Singular Masculine Feminine Neuter Nominative ένας μια ένα Genitive ενός μιας ενός Accusative ένα(ν) μια(ν) ένα

The feminine singular forms differ only in pronunciation but not in usage or anything else.

docs.title: Declension
docs.text: [[Nouns|Nouns]] in [[./index|Modern Greek]] change their form to indicate their [[TODO|case]] and [[TODO|number]]. [[Nouns|Nouns]] are grouped into declensions depending on which set of endings they use. The declension to which a [[Nouns|noun]] belongs is largely determined by its [[TODO|gender]] and [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]], but, sometimes, even this information is insufficient to draw a conclusion and you have to check with a dictionary. It is also useful to classify [[Nouns|nouns]] by the position of the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] in their [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]]: oxytone on the last [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]], paroxytone on the second-to-last [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] and proparoxytone on the third-to-last [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]].

docs.title: Masculine Nouns
docs.text:
[[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] ending in -ος can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]], [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]]: - [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Oxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] remain such throughout the entire declension. - [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Paroxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] also remain such throughout the entire declension. - Most [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in both [[TODO|genitive]] forms and the [[TODO|accusative]] [[TODO|plural]]. However, some nouns, especially compounds, remain [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] throughout.

Masculine Nouns Ending in -ος Singular Plural Nominative -ος -οι Genitive -ου -ων Accusative -ο -ους Vocative -ε -οι Example: Masculine Nouns Ending in -ος

Singular Plural Nominative καιρός καιροί Genitive καιρού καιρών Accusative καιρό καιρούς Vocative καιρέ καιροί

Singular Plural Nominative κόσμος κόσμοι Genitive κόσμου κόσμων Accusative κόσμο κόσμους Vocative κόσμε κόσμοι

Singular Plural Nominative άνθρωπος άνθρωποι Genitive ανθρώπου ανθρώπων Accusative άνθρωπο ανθρώπους Vocative άνθρωπε άνθρωποι

καλόγερος ("monk") Singular Plural Nominative καλόγερος καλόγεροι Genitive καλόγερου καλόγερων Accusative καλόγερο καλόγερους Vocative καλόγερε καλόγεροι

[[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ης are divided into several subgroups depending on the ending of their [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]]: -ες, -ηδες, -ητες, -εις. - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ης that don't add anything before the -ες of their [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]]. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Oxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] remain such throughout. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Paroxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] remain such except in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] where they become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]]. - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ης that add -ηδ- before the -ες of the [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]]. - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ης that add -ητ- before the -ες of the [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]]. They keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] thoughout except in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]], where it moves to the -η- of the ending. - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ης with [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] in -εις are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] and keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] throughout.

Masculine Nouns in -ης Singular Plural Nominative -ης -ες -ηδες -ητες -εις Genitive -η -ων -ηδων -ήτων -εων Accusative -η -ες -ηδες -ητες -εις Vocative -η -ες -ηδες -ητες -εις Example: Parisyllabic Masculine Nouns Ending in -ης, -ες

μαθητής Singular Plural Nominative μαθητής μαθητές Genitive μαθητή μαθητών Accusative μαθητή μαθητές Vocative μαθητή μαθητές

πελάτης Singular Plural Nominative πελάτης πελάτες Genitive πελάτη πελατών Accusative πελάτη πελάτες Vocative πελάτη πελάτες

Example: Masculine Nouns Ending in -ης, -ηδες

Singular Plural Nominative μερακλής μερακλήδες Genitive μερακλή μερακλήδων Accusative μερακλή μερακλήδες Vocative μερακλή μερακλήδες

Singular Plural Nominative μπακάλης μπακάληδες Genitive μπακάλη μπακάληδων Accusative μπακάλη μπακάληδες Vocative μπακάλη μπακάληδες

Example: Masculine Nouns Ending in -ης, -ητες

γόης ("charmer") Singular Plural Nominative γόης γόητες Genitive γόη γοήτων Accusative γόη γόητες Vocative γόη γόητες

Example: Masculine Nouns Ending in -ης, -εις

Singular Plural Nominative λάτρης λάτρεις Genitive λάτρη λάτρεων Accusative λάτρη λάτρεις Vocative λάτρη λάτρεις

[[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]] in -aς are divided into a few subgroups depending on the ending of their [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]]: -ες, -αδες, -ηδες or -εíς: - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ας that don't add a [[TODO|syllable]] before the -ες of the [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]]. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Paroxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] with two [[TODO|syllables]] remain such except in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]], where they become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]]. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Paroxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] with more than two [[TODO|syllables]] remain such throughout. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Proparoxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]]. - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ας that add -αδ- before the -ες of the [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] and become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in the [[TODO|plural]] because of the added [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]]. - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ας that add -ηδ- before the -ες of the [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] and become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] in the [[TODO|plural]] because of the added [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]]. - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -έας that have a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] in -εíς are [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in all [[TODO|singular]] forms and in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]]. In the rest of the [[TODO|plural]] forms, they are [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]]. In the [[TODO|singular]], they decline like all other [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ας but in the [[TODO|plural]] the ending replaces the final -ε of the stem.

Masculine Nouns Ending in -ας Singular Plural Nominative -ας -ες -άδες -ηδες -εíς Genitive -α -ων -άδων -ηδων -έων Accusative -α -ες -άδες -ηδες -εíς Vocative -α -ες -άδες -ηδες -εíς Example: Masculine Nouns Ending in -ας, -ες

Declension of άντρας Singular Plural Nominative άντρας άντρες Genitive άντρα αντρών Accusative άντρα άντρες Vocative άντρα άντρες

Declension of κανόνας Singular Plural Nominative κανόνας κανόνες Genitive κανόνα κανόνων Accusative κανόνα κανόνες Vocative κανόνα κανόνες

Declension of ελέφαντας Singular Plural Nominative ελέφαντας ελέφαντες Genitive ελέφαντα ελεφάντων Accusative ελέφαντα ελέφαντες Vocative ελέφαντα ελέφαντες

Example: Masculine Nouns in -άς, -άδες

μπαμπάς ("dad") Singular Plural Nominative μπαμπάς μπαμπάδες Genitive μπαμπά μπαμπάδων Accusative μπαμπά μπαμπάδες Vocative μπαμπά μπαμπάδες

Example: Masculine Nouns Ending in -ας, -ηδες

Declension of αέρας Singular Plural Nominative αέρας αέρηδες Genitive αέρα αέρηδων Accusative αέρα αέρηδες Vocative αέρα αέρηδες

Example: Masculine Nouns Ending in -έας, -είς

Declension of γραμματέας Singular Plural Nominative γραμματέας γραμματείς Genitive γραμματέα γραμματέων Accusative γραμματέα γραμματείς Vocative γραμματέα γραμματείς

[[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ες are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] and remain such throughout the [[TODO|singular]] but become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in the [[TODO|plural]] due to the added [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]].

Masculine Nouns in -ές, -έδες Singular Plural Nominative -ές -έδες Genitive -έ -έδων Accusative -έ -έδες Vocative -έ -έδες Example: Masculine Nouns in -ές, -έδες

καφές ("coffee") Singular Plural Nominative καφές καφέδες Genitive καφέ καφέδων Accusative καφέ καφέδες Vocative καφέ καφέδες

[[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ους are divided into two groups depending on the ending of their [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]]: -οι or -ουδες. - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ους with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] in -οι can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] and both types remain as such in all forms. - [[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ους with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] in -ουδες are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] in their [[TODO|singular]] forms and become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in the [[TODO|plural]] forms due to the added [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]].

Masculine Nouns in -ους Singular Plural Nominative -ους -οι -ούδες Genitive -ου -ων -ούδων Accusative -ου -ους -ούδες Vocative -ου -οι -ούδες Example: Masculine Nouns in -ους, -οι

νους ("mind") Singular Plural Nominative νους νοι Genitive νου νων Accusative νου νους Vocative νου νοι

απόπλους ("ship departure") Singular Plural Nominative απόπλους απόπλοι Genitive απόπλου απόπλων Accusative απόπλου απόπλους Vocative απόπλου απόπλοι

Example: Masculine Nouns in -ούς, -ούδες

παππούς ("grandpa") Singular Plural Nominative παππούς παππούδες Genitive παππού παππούδων Accusative παππού παππούδες Vocative παππού παππούδες

[[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -υς can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]]. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Paroxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] throughout, while [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] move it one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right in the [[TODO|plural]].

Masculine Nouns in -υς Singular Plural Nominative -υς -εις Genitive -υ -εων Accusative -υ -εις Vocative -υ -εις Example: Masculine Nouns Ending in -υς

πήχυς (a measure of length) Singular Plural Nominative πήχυς πήχεις Genitive πήχυ πήχεων Accusative πήχυ πήχεις Vocative πήχυ πήχεις

πέλεκυς ("double-headed axe") Singular Plural Nominative πέλεκυς πελέκεις Genitive πέλεκυ πελέκεων Accusative πέλεκυ πελέκεις Vocative πέλεκυ πελέκεις

Exception: The Irregular Noun "μυς" ("muscle")

The [[Nouns|noun]] "μυς" ("muscle") is declined as follows:

μυς ("muscle") Singular Plural Nominative μυς μύες Genitive μυός μυών Accusative μυ μυς Vocative μυ μύες

[[TODO|Masculine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ωρ are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in the [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]]. They keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] in all forms except for the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] where it moves one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right.

Masculine Nouns Ending in -ωρ Singular Plural Nominative -ωρ -ορες Genitive -ορος -όρων Accusative -ορα -ορες Vocative -ωρ -ορες Example: Masculine Nouns Ending in -ωρ

μέντωρ ("mentor") Singular Plural Nominative μέντωρ μέντορες Genitive μέντορος μεντόρων Accusative μέντορα μέντορες Vocative μέντωρ μέντορες

docs.title: Feminine Nouns
docs.text:
[[TODO|Feminine]] [[TODO|nouns]] with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]] in -α can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]], [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]]. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Oxytone]] ones remain such in all forms. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Paroxytone]] [[TODO|nouns]] remain such except possibly in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]], where some become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]]. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Proparoxytone]] [[TODO|nouns]] remain such in all forms except in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]], where some become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]], while others [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]].

Feminine Nouns in -α Singular Plural Nominative -α -ες Genitive -ας -ων Accusative -α -ες Vocative -α -ες Example: Feminine Nouns in -α, -ες

φορά ("time, occurrence)" Singular Plural Nominative φορά φορές Genitive φοράς φορών Accusative φορά φορές Vocative φορά φορές

ελπίδα ("hope") Singular Plural Nominative ελπίδα ελπίδες Genitive ελπίδας ελπίδων Accusative ελπίδα ελπίδες Vocative ​ελπίδα ελπίδες

ώρα ("hour") Singular Plural Nominative ώρα ώρες Genitive ώρας ωρών Accusative ώρα ώρες Vocative ​ώρα ώρες

θάλασσα ("sea") Singular Plural Nominative θάλασσα θάλασσες Genitive θάλασσας θαλασσών Accusative θάλασσα θάλασσες Vocative θάλασσα θάλασσες

ποσότητα ("quantity", "amount") Singular Plural Nominative ποσότητα ποσότητες Genitive ποσότητας ποσοτήτων Accusative ποσότητα ποσότητες Vocative ποσότητα ποσότητες

Exception: Feminine Nouns in -ά

Some [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] [[TODO|feminine]] [[TODO|nouns]] in -ά add -αδ- in before the endings of the [[TODO|plural]]. The [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] then falls on this -αδ-.

μαμά ("mom") Singular Plural Nominative μαμά μαμάδες Genitive μαμάς μαμάδων Accusative μαμά μαμάδες Vocative μαμά μαμάδες

γιαγιά ("grandmother") Singular Plural Nominative γιαγιά γιαγιάδες Genitive γιαγιάς γιαγιάδων Accusative γιαγιά γιαγιάδες Vocative γιαγιά γιαγιάδες

[[TODO|Feminine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -η are divided into two subgroups depending on the ending of their [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]]: -ες or -εις. - [[TODO|Feminine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -η with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] in -ες can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]], [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]]. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Oxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] remain such throughout, while [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]]. Both of these types have a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] in just -ων. Some [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] have a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] in just -ων, while others in -εων. Those with a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] in just -ων become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] in this form, while those with a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] in -εων remain [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] (but in doing so move the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right). - [[TODO|Feminine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -η with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] in -εις can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]]. The former keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] throughout, while the latter move it one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right in all [[TODO|plural]] forms.

Feminine Nouns in -η Singular Plural Nominative -η -ες -εις Genitive -ης -ων, -εων -εων Accusative -η -ες -εις Vocative ​-η -ες -εις Example: Feminine Nouns in -η, -ες

ψυχή ("soul") Singular Plural Nominative ψυχή ψυχές Genitive ψυχής ψυχών Accusative ψυχή ψυχές Vocative ψυχή ψυχές

αγάπη ("love") Singular Plural Nominative αγάπη αγάπες Genitive αγάπης αγαπών Accusative αγάπη αγάπες Vocative αγάπη αγάπες

κάμαρη ("cabin") Singular Plural Nominative κάμαρη κάμαρες Genitive κάμαρης καμαρών Accusative κάμαρη κάμαρες Vocative κάμαρη κάμαρες

ζάχαρη ("sugar") Singular Plural Nominative ζάχαρη ζάχαρες Genitive ζάχαρης ζαχάρεων Accusative ζάχαρη ζάχαρες Vocative ζάχαρη ζάχαρες

Example: Feminine Nouns in -η, -εις

πόλη ("city") Singular Plural Nominative πόλη πόλεις Genitive πόλης πόλεων Accusative πόλη πόλεις Vocative πόλη πόλεις

κυβέρνηση ("government") Singular Plural Nominative κυβέρνηση κυβερνήσεις Genitive κυβέρνησης κυβερνήσεων Accusative κυβέρνηση κυβερνήσεις Vocative κυβέρνηση κυβερνήσεις

[[TODO|Feminine]] [[TODO|nouns]] in -ος can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]], [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]]. [[Phonology#Accent|Oxytone]] and [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] ones remain such throughout. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Proparoxytone]] [[TODO|nouns]] become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in both [[TODO|genitive]] forms and in the [[TODO|accusative]] [[TODO|plural]].

Feminine Nouns Ending in -ος Singular Plural Nominative -ος -οι Genitive -ου -ων Accusative -ο -ους Vocative ​-ε, (-ο) -οι Example: Feminine Nouns in -ος

οδός ("street") Singular Plural Nominative οδός οδοί Genitive οδού οδών Accusative οδό οδούς Vocative οδέ οδοί

παρθένος ("virgin") Singular Plural Nominative παρθένος παρθένοι Genitive παρθένου παρθένων Accusative παρθένο παρθένους Vocative παρθένε, παρθένο παρθένοι

άβυσσος ("abyss") Singular Plural Nominative άβυσσος άβυσσοι Genitive αβύσσου αβύσσων Accusative άβυσσο αβύσσους Vocative άβυσσε, άβυσσο άβυσσοι

[[TODO|Feminine]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ου are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] in the [[TODO|singular]] and [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in the [[TODO|plural]].

Feminine Nouns in -ού Singular Plural Nominative -ού -ούδες Genitive -ούς -ούδων Accusative -ού -ούδες Vocative ​-ού -ούδες Example: Feminine Nouns in -ού

αλεπού ("fox") Singular Plural Nominative αλεπού αλεπούδες Genitive αλεπούς αλεπούδων Accusative αλεπού αλεπούδες Vocative αλεπού αλεπούδες

Feminine Nouns in -έας, -είς Singular Plural Nominative -έας -είς Genitive -έως -έων Accusative -έα -είς Vocative -έα -είς Example: Feminine Nouns in -έας, -είς

γραμματέας ("secretary") Singular Plural Nominative γραμματέας γραμματείς Genitive γραμματέως γραμματέων Accusative γραμματέα γραμματείς Vocative γραμματέα γραμματείς

Feminine Nouns in -ίας, -ίες Singular Plural Nominative -ίας -ίες Genitive -ία(ς) -ιών Accusative -ία -ίες Vocative -ία -ίες Example: Feminine Nouns in -ίας, -ίες

ταμίας ("cashier") Singular Plural Nominative ταμίας ταμίες Genitive ταμία, ταμίας ταμιών Accusative ταμία ταμίες Vocative ταμία ταμίες

docs.title: Neuter Nouns
docs.text:
Important: Nominative, Accusative and Vocative of Neuter Nouns

The [[TODO|accusative]] and [[TODO|vocative]] of [[TODO|neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] are always identical to the [[TODO|nominative]] in the respective [[TODO|number]].

[[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] ending in -ο have a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ου. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Oxytone]] and [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] of this [[Nouns#Declension|declension]] keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] in all forms. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Proparoxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]], however, may become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in the [[TODO|genitive]]. Furthermore, some [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] can be both [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] and [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in the [[TODO|genitive]].

Neuter Nouns in -ο Singular Plural Nominative -ο -α Genitive -ου -ων Accusative =Nom =Nom Vocative =Nom =Nom Example: Neuter Nouns in -ο

νερό ("water") Singular Plural Nominative νερό νερά Genitive νερού νερών Accusative νερό νερά Vocative νερό νερά

βιβλίο ("book") Singular Plural Nominative βιβλίο βιβλία Genitive βιβλίου βιβλίων Accusative βιβλίο βιβλία Vocative βιβλίο βιβλία

κάρβουνο ("coal") Singular Plural Nominative κάρβουνο κάρβουνα Genitive κάρβουνου κάρβουνων Accusative κάρβουνο κάρβουνα Vocative κάρβουνο κάρβουνα

άτομο ("individual", "person"; "atom") Singular Plural Nominative άτομο άτομα Genitive ατόμου ατόμων Accusative άτομο άτομα Vocative άτομο άτομα

[[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] ending in -ι have a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ια, a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ιου and a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] in -ιών. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Oxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] remain such throughout all forms. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Paroxytone]] ones keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] in all forms, except in the [[TODO|genitive]] where they become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]]. There are no [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] of this group.

Neuter Nouns in -ι Singular Plural Nominative -ι -ια Genitive -ιου -ιων Accusative =Nom =Nom Vocative =Nom =Nom Example: Neuter Nouns in -ι

παιδί ("child") Singular Plural Nominative παιδί παιδιά Genitive παιδιού παιδιών Accusative παιδί παιδιά Vocative παιδί παιδιά

αγόρι ("book") Singular Plural Nominative αγόρι αγόρια Genitive αγοριού αγοριών Accusative αγόρι αγόρια Vocative αγόρι αγόρια

Exception: πρωί ("morning")

The noun πρωί ("morning") is declined as follows:

πρωί ("morning") Singular Plural Nominative πρωί πρωινά Genitive πρωινού πρωινών Accusative πρωί πρωινά Vocative πρωί πρωινά

Exception: Nouns in -υ / -ι

The nouns βράδυ ("evening"), δίχτυ ("net"), στάχυ ("ear of corn") can be spelled either with -υ or -ι. Their other forms are normally spelled with -ι-, though.

βράδυ ("evening") Singular Plural Nominative βράδυ βράδια Genitive βραδιού βραδιών Accusative βράδυ βράδια Vocative βράδυ βράδια

However, the noun δάκρυ ("tear") is spelled with υ in all its forms and has a different stress:

δάκρυ ("tear") Singular Plural Nominative δάκρυ δάκρυα Genitive δακρύου δακρύων Accusative δάκρυ δάκρυα Vocative δάκρυ δάκρυα

Exception: Neuter Nouns in -άι and -όι

Neuter nouns ending in -άι and -όι add -γ- before all endings except the [[TODO|nominative]] / [[TODO|accusative]] / [[TODO|vocative]] [[TODO|singular]].

τσάι ("tea") Singular Plural Nominative τσάι τσάγια Genitive τσαγιού τσαγιών Accusative τσάι τσάγια Vocative τσάι τσάγια

Exception: Diminutives in -άκι and -ούλι

Diminutive nouns ending in -άκι and -ούλι have no [[TODO|genitive]] forms.

παιδάκι ("little child") Singular Plural Nominative παιδάκι παιδάκια Genitive Accusative παιδάκι παιδάκια Vocative παιδάκι παιδάκια

[[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] ending in -ος are divided into two groups based on the ending of their [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]]: -η or -ότα. - All [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ος have a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ότος, a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] in -ότα and a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] in -ότων. This pattern is quite rare. - All [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] and [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ος have a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ους, a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] in -ων and a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] in -η. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Paroxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]]. [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|Proparoxytone]] [[Nouns|nouns]] become [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] and [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] in all other [[TODO|plural]] forms and in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]].

Neuter Nouns in -ος Singular Plural Nominative -ός -ος -ότα -η Genitive -ότος -ους -ότων -ων Accusative =Nom =Nom =Nom =Nom Vocative =Nom =Nom =Nom =Nom Example: Neuter Nouns Ending in -ός, -ότα

γεγονός ("fact") Singular Plural Nominative γεγονός γεγονότα Genitive γεγονότος γεγονότων Accusative γεγονός γεγονότα Vocative ​γεγονός γεγονότα

Example: Neuter Nouns in -ος, -η

δάσος ("forest") Singular Plural Nominative δάσος δάση Genitive δάσους δασών Accusative δάσος δάση Vocative δάσος δάση

μέγεθος ("size") Singular Plural Nominative μέγεθος μεγέθη Genitive μεγέθους μεγεθών Accusative μέγεθος μεγέθη Vocative μέγεθος μεγέθη

[[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] ending in -α have a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ατος, [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] in -άτων and other [[TODO|plural]] forms in -ατα. They can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]]. Their [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]] is always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]], while their [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] is always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]]. The rest of the [[TODO|plural]] forms are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|proparoxytone]].

Neuter Nouns Ending in -α Singular Plural Nominative -α -ατα Genitive -ατος -άτων Accusative -α -ατα Vocative ​-α -ατα Example: Neuter Nouns in -α

χρώμα ("color") Singular Plural Nominative χρώμα χρώματα Genitive χρώματος χρωμάτων Accusative χρώμα χρώματα Vocative χρώμα χρώματα

πρόβλημα ("problem") Singular Plural Nominative πρόβλημα προβλήματα Genitive προβλήματος προβλημάτων Accusative πρόβλημα προβλήματα Vocative πρόβλημα προβλήματα

Exception: The Noun "γάλα" ("milk")

The [[Nouns|noun]] "γάλα" ("milk") is declined as follows:

γάλα ("milk") Singular Plural Nominative γάλα γάλατα Genitive γάλακτος γαλάκτων Accusative γάλα γάλατα Vocative γάλα γάλατα

[[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -υ which are not alternative spellings of those in -ι have a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|plural]] in -ατα. They are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] and keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] throughout, except in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]] where it moves one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right.

Neuter Nouns in -υ, -ατα Singular Plural Nominative -υ -ατα Genitive -ατος -άτων Accusative -υ -ατα Vocative -υ -ατα Example: Neuter Nouns in -υ, -ατα

δόρυ ("spear") Singular Plural Nominative δόρυ δόρατα Genitive δόρατος δοράτων Accusative δόρυ δόρατα Vocative δόρυ δόρατα

Exception: The Noun "οξύ" ("acid")

The [[Nouns|noun]] "οξύ" ("acid") is declined as follows:

οξύ ("acid") Singular Plural Nominative οξύ οξέα Genitive οξέος οξέων Accusative οξύ οξέα Vocative οξύ οξέα

Exception: The Noun "ήμισυ" ("half")

The [[Nouns|noun]] "ήμισυ" ("half") is declined as follows:

ήμισυ ("half") Singular Plural Nominative ήμισυ ημίσεα Genitive ημίσεος ημίσεων Accusative ήμισυ ημίσεα Vocative ήμισυ ημίσεα

[[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ας are always [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] and keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] throughout, except in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]], where it moves one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right.

Neuter Nouns in -ας Singular Plural Nominative -ας -ατος Genitive -ατος -άτων Accusative -ας -ατα Vocative ​-ας -ατα Example: Neuter Nouns in -ας

κρέας ("meat") Singular Plural Nominative κρέας κρέατα Genitive κρέατος κρεάτων Accusative κρέας κρέατα Vocative ​κρέας κρέατα

[[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -ως can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]]. The former keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] throughout, except in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]], where it moves one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right. The latter keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] throughout, except in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]], where it moves one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right.

Neuter Nouns in -ως Singular Plural Nominative -ως -ωτα Genitive -ωτος -ώτων Accusative =Nom =Nom Vocative =Nom =Nom Example: Neuter Nouns in -ως

φως ("light") Singular Plural Nominative φως φώτα Genitive φωτός φώτων Accusative φως φώτα Vocative φως φώτα

λυκόφως ("dusk") Singular Plural Nominative λυκόφως λυκόφωτα Genitive λυκόφωτος λυκοφώτων Accusative λυκόφως λυκόφωτα Vocative ​λυκόφως λυκόφωτα

[[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ον are divided into two subgroups depending on the ending of their [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]]: -ου or -οντος. - All [[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ον and a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ου are [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]] and remain such throughout. - [[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] with a [[TODO|nominative]] [[TODO|singular]] in -ον and a [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|singular]] in -οντος can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]]. The former keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] throughout, while the latter move it one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]].

Neuter Nouns in -ον, -ου Singular Plural Nominative -ον -α -οντα Genitive -ου -οντος -ων -όντων Accusative =Nom =Nom =Nom Vocative =Nom =Nom =Nom Example: Neuter Nouns Ending in -ον, -ου

μέσον ("intermediary") Singular Plural Nominative μέσον μέσα Genitive μέσου μέσων Accusative μέσον μέσα Vocative μέσον μέσα

Example: Neuter Nouns in -ον, -οντος

προσόν ("qualification") Singular Plural Nominative προσόν προσόντα Genitive προσόντος προσόντων Accusative προσόν προσόντα Vocative προσόν προσόντα

ενδιαφέρον ("interest") Singular Plural Nominative ενδιαφέρον ενδιαφέροντα Genitive ενδιαφέροντος ενδιαφερόντων Accusative ενδιαφέρον ενδιαφέροντα Vocative ​ενδιαφέρον ενδιαφέροντα

[[TODO|Neuter]] [[Nouns|nouns]] in -εν and -αν decline in the same way with the only exception being the difference in the vowels: ε or α. They can be either [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|oxytone]] or [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|paroxytone]]. The former keep the [[Orthography and Phonology#Accent|stress]] on the same [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] throughout, while the latter move it one [[Orthography and Phonology#Syllabification|syllable]] to the right in the [[TODO|genitive]] [[TODO|plural]].

Neuter Nouns in -εν / -αν Singular Plural Nominative -εν -αν -εντα -αντα Genitive -εντος -αντος -έντων -άντων Accusative =Nom =Nom =Nom =Nom Vocative =Nom =Nom =Nom =Nom Example: Neuter Nouns in -εν

ανακοινωθέν ("announcement") Singular Plural Nominative ανακοινωθέν ανακοινωθέντα Genitive ανακοινωθέντος ανακοινωθέντων Accusative ανακοινωθέν ανακοινωθέντα Vocative ​ανακοινωθέν ανακοινωθέντα

φωνήεν ("vowel") Singular Plural Nominative φωνήεν φωνήεντα Genitive φωνήεντος φωνηέντων Accusative φωνήεν φωνήεντα Vocative φωνήεν φωνήεντα

Example: Neuter Nouns in -αν

συμβάν ("event", "occurrence") Singular Plural Nominative συμβάν συμβάντα Genitive συμβάντος συμβάντων Accusative συμβάν συμβάντα Vocative ​συμβάν συμβάντα

σύμπαν ("universe") Singular Plural Nominative σύμπαν σύμπαντα Genitive σύμπαντος συμπάντων Accusative σύμπαν σύμπαντα Vocative ​σύμπαν σύμπαντα

Neuter Nouns in -α, -ακτος Singular Plural Nominative -α -ατα Genitive -ακτος -άκτων Accusative -α -ατα Vocative ​-α -ατα

The stress in the nominative singular of these nouns is always on the penult and remains on the same vowel in all forms except for the genitive plural where it moves to the "α" of the ending.

Example: Neuter Nouns Ending in -α / -ακτος

Declension of γάλα Singular Plural Nominative γάλα γάλατα Genitive γάλακτος γαλάκτων Accusative γάλα γάλατα Vocative γάλα γάλατα

docs.title: Cardinal Numerals
docs.text:
Cardinal numerals indicate count, size, amount, etc.

Fundamental Cardinal Numerals Value Name 0 μηδέν 1 ένας 2 δύο, δυο 3 τρεις 4 τέσσερις 5 πέντε 6 έξι 7 επτά, εφτά 8 οκτώ, οχτώ 9 εννέα, εννιά 10 δέκα 11 ένδεκα, έντεκα 12 δώδεκα 13 δεκατρεις 14 δεκατέσσερις 15 δεκαπέντε 16 δεκαέξι, δεκάξι 17 δεκαεπτά, δεκαεφτά 18 δεκαοκτώ, δεκαοχτώ 19 δεκαεννέα, δεκαεννιά 20 είκοσι 21 είκοσι ένας 30 τριάντα 40 σαράντα 50 πενήντα 60 εξήντα 70 εβδομήντα 80 ογδόντα 90 ενενήντα 100 εκατό(ν) 200 διακόσια 300 τριακόσια 400 τετρακόσια 500 πέντακόσια 600 εξακόσια 700 επτακόσια, εφτακόσια 800 οκτακόσια, οχτακόσια 900 εννιακόσια 1000 χίλια 2000 δύο χιλιάδες 3000 τρεις χιλιάδες 1 000 000 ένα εκατομμύρια 1 000 000 000 ένα δισεκατομμύρια

The parts marked in italics are declined for [[TODO|gender]], [[TODO|case]] and [[TODO|number]].

The cardinals "ένας", "τρεις" and "τέσσερις" are declined as follows:

ένας, μια, ένα Masculine Feminine Neuter Nominative ένας μια, μία ένα Genitive ενός μιας ενός Accusative ένα(ν) μια(ν), μία(ν) ένα τρεις, τρία Plural Masculine Feminine Neuter Nominative τρεις τρία Genitive τριών Accusative τρεις τρία τέσσερις, τέσσερα Plural Masculine Feminine Neuter Nominative τέσσερις τέσσερα Genitive τεσσάρων Accusative τέσσερις τέσσερα

All hundres ending in -κόσια are declined like the [[TODO|plural]] of [[Adjectives|adjectives]] in -ος, -α / -η, -ο.

Constructing the numbers until 2000 is done by just listing their components, very similar to English. However, the word "and" is not used in Greek and there are a few peculiarities: - When 2 occurs as a component in a number, it is always the stressed form "δύο". - When 100 occurs as a component in a number, it is always the full form "εκτόν". - When declinable numerals occur as components, they are still declined. - After 1999, the word "χιλίαδες" is used and the numeral accompanying it must be declined for the feminine.

Example: Composite Cardinal Numerals

528 λουλούδια - πεντακόσια είκοσι οκτώ λουλούδια

521 λουλουδιού - πεντακόσιων είκοσι ένος λουλουδιών

2154 νομισμάτων - δύο χιλίαδες εκτόν πενήντα τεσσαρών νομισμάτων

docs.title: Orthography
docs.text:
The writing system used by Modern Greek is an alphabet with 24 letters.

Letter Greek Name English Name Phonemic Value Α α άλφα alpha /a/ Β β βήτα beta /v/ Γ γ γάμμα gamma /ɣ/ Δ δ δέλτα delta /ð/ Ε ε έψιλον epsilon /e/ Ζ ζ ζήτα zeta /z/ Η η ήτα eta /i/ Θ θ θήτα theta /θ/ Ι ι ιώτα iota /i/ Κ κ κάππα kappa /k/ Λ λ λάμδα lambda /l/ Μ μ μυ mu /m/ Ν ν νυ nu /n/ Ξ ξ ξι xi /ks/ Ο ο όμικρον omicron /o/ Π π πι pi /p/ Ρ ρ ρο rho /ɾ/ Σ σ ς σίγμα sigma /s/ Τ τ ταυ tau /t/ Υ υ ύψιλον upsilon /i/ Χ χ χι chi /x/ Ψ ψ ψι psi /ps/ Ω ω ωμέγα omega /o/

The letter sigma is written as σ in the middle of words and as ς at the end of words.

docs.title: Diagraphs
docs.text:
There is a set of letter combinations, known as digraphs which are used to represent sounds other than what their constituent letters usually would.

Modern Greek Digraphs Digraph Pronunciation Example ΑΙ, αι /e/ αίμα [ˈe.ma](blood) ΕΙ, ει /i/ ειρήνη [iˈri.ni](peace) ΟΙ, οι οικογένεια [i.koˈʝe.ni.a](family) ΥΙ, υι υιός [iˈos](son) ΑΥ, αυ /av/ before a vowel or voiced consonant αυγό [avˈɣo](egg) /af/ otherwise αυτός [afˈtos](he) ΕΥ, ευ /ev/ before a vowel or voiced consonant Ευρώπη [evˈro.pi](Europe) /ef/ otherwise ευχαριστώ [ef.xa.riˈsto](thank you) ΗΥ, ηυ /iv/ before a vowel or voiced consonant ηύρα [ˈiv.ra](he/she found) /if/ otherwise ηύξησε [ˈif.ksi.se](he/she increased) ΟΥ, ου /u/ ουρανός [u.raˈnos](sky) ΓΓ, γγ [ŋɟ] but often reduced to [ɡ] in informal speech άγγελος [ˈaɲ.ɟe.los](angel) ΓΚ, γκ [ɡ] word-initially and in some loanwords γκρεμός [ɡreˈmos](cliff) [ŋɡ] otherwise, but often reduced to [ɡ] in informal speech αγκώνας [aŋˈɡo.nas](elbow) ΓΞ, γξ [ŋks] σφίγξ [sfiŋks](sphinx) ΓΧ, γχ [ŋx] before /a/, /o/, /u/ έλεγχος [ˈe.leŋ.xos](check, control) [ɲç] before /e/, /i/ σύγχυση [ˈsiɲ.çi.si](confusion) Μπ, μπ [b] word-initially and in loanwords μπάλα [ˈba.la](ball) [mb] otherwise, but often reduced to [b] in informal speech λάμπα [ˈlam.ba](lamp) Ντ, ντ [d] word-initially and in loanwords ντομάτα [doˈma.ta](tomato) [nd] otherwise, but often reduced to [d] in informal speech πάντα [ˈpan.da](always) ΤΖ, τζ [d͡z] τζάκι [ˈd͡za.ci](fireplace)

Sometimes, the letter combinations αι, ει, οι, υι, αυ, ευ, ηυ, ου are not meant to be treated as digraphs and their letters are supposed to be pronounced separately. This is indicated by placing a diaeresis (¨) on the second letter. If the stress falls on the first letter of such a combination, then the acute accent is written on it and the diaeresis (¨) is omitted (e.g. "τσάι" and not "τσάϊ").

docs.title: Accent Marks
docs.text:
The acute accent ´ is used to mark accented syllables in polysyllabic words and is placed on the vowel of said syllables. If the vowel is an uppercase letter, then the accent is placed up and to the left of it. If the letter is lowercase, then the accent is placed on top of it. In digraphs, the second letter takes the accent.

Example: Acute Accent for Stress

είμαι /'i.me̞/

αύριο /'av.ɾi.o/

The acute accent can also appear in monosyllabic words to distinguish between words which would otherwise be written in the same way.

Example: Acute Accent as Distinguisher

πώς (how?, what?) <-> πως (that)

ή (or) <-> η (the)

The diaeresis ¨ is used to indicate that two consecutive letters should not be treated as a digraph. It is placed on the second letter.

docs.title: Vowels
docs.text:
Modern Greek has five [[TODO|vowel]] [[TODO|phonemes]].

Modern Greek Vowel Phonemes Front Central Back Close /i/ η, ι, υ, ει, οι, υι /u/ ου Mid /e/ ε, αι /o/ ο, ω Open /a/ α

The [[TODO|vowel]] [[TODO|phonemes]] are actualized by the following phones: - /a/ as the [[TODO|near-open central vowel]] [ɐ]; - /i/ as the [[TODO|close front unrounded vowel]] [i]; - /u/ as the [[TODO|close back rounded vowel]] [u]; - /e/ as the [[TODO|mid front unrounded vowel]] [e̞]; - /o/ as the [[TODO|mid back rounded vowel]] [o̞].

There is no distinction between long and short vowels.

The phoneme /u/ is actualized as the non-syllabic consonant [[TODO|allophone]] [w] when simultaneously unstressed and preceded by a vowel.

The [[TODO|phoneme]] /i/ also has a few [[TODO|consonantal]] [[TODO|allophones]] which occur when it is unstressed. - The [[TODO|allophone]] [j] occurs when an unstressed /i/ is preceded by a vowel: λέει [lej] ("it says"), αϊτός [aj.'tos] ("eagle"); - The [[TODO|allophone]] [ʝ] occurs when an unstressed /i/ is preceded by a voiced consonant: δυο [ðʝo] ("two"), παιδιά [pe.'ðʝa] ("children"). - The [[TODO|allophone]] [ç] occurs when an unstressed /i/ is preceded by a voiceless consonant: φωτιά [fo.ˈtça] ("fire"), ελάφια [eˈlaf.ça] ("deer"); - The [[TODO|allophone]] [ɲ] occurs when an unstressed /i/ is preceded by the consonant /m/: μια [mɲa] ("one").

docs.title: Consonants
docs.text:
Modern Greek Consonant Phonemes Bilabial Labiodental Dental Alveolar Palatal Velar Nasal /m/ μ /n/ ν Plosive /p/ π/b/ μπ /t/ τ/d/ ντ /k/ κ/g/ γκ Fricative /f/ φ/v/ β /θ/ θ/ð/ δ /s/ σ, ς/z/ ζ /x/ χ/ɣ/ γ Affricate /ts/ τσ/dz/ τζ Tap /ɾ/ ρ Lateral Approximant /l/ λ

Info: Phonetic Changes before /e/ and /i/

The following [[TODO|phonemes]] change their actualization when followed by the Orthography and Phonology /e/ and /i/:

  • /k/ is actualized as [c];
  • /g/ is actualized as [ɟ];
  • /x/ is actualized as [ç];
  • /ɣ/ is actualized as [ʝ].

This is true both within the bounds of individual words as well as across word boundaries.

Example: Phonetic Changes before /e/ and /i/

κερί [ce'ri] ("candle")

άγγελος [ˈaŋ.ɟe.los] ("angel", "messenger")

χέρι [ˈçe.ɾi] ("hand")

γέρος [ˈʝeɾos] ("old man")

Info: [s] -> [z]

The [[TODO|phoneme]] /s/ turns into /z/ when followed by a voiced [[TODO|phoneme]] (/v/, /ɣ/, /ʝ/, /) or one of /m/, /ɾ/ and /n/.

This is true both within the bounds of individual words as well as across word boundaries.

Example

σβήνω ['zvi.no]

κόσμος ['koz.mos]

τους δύο [tuz 'ði.o]

Info: [n p] -> [mb], [n t] -> [nd], [n k] -> [ŋg]

Across word boundaries, the [[TODO|phoneme]] combinations [n p], [n t] and [n k] change to [nd], [n k] and [ŋg[, respectively.

Example

τον πόνο /tom.'bo.no/

τον τόνο /ton.'do.no/

την καρδιά /tiŋ.gaɾ.'ðia/

docs.title: Accent
docs.text:
Similarly to English, Modern Greek has a stress accent system in which every word has a syllable pronounced slightly louder and longer than the others. This syllable is marked by an acute accent.

Important: The Antepenultimate Rule

The stress of a word can only be in one of three possible positions:

  • oxytone - on the ultima (last syllable);
  • paroxytone - on the penult (second-to-last syllable);
  • proparoxytone - on the antepenult (third-to-last syllable).

This rule is never broken. It is so strong that it can force the stress to move in inflected forms of the same word, lest it is broken.

Info: Derived Stress

In certain situations, a single word may have two accented syllables:

  • If a noun / adjective / adverb / verb / preposition has a proparoxytone accent and is followed by a weak personal pronoun or a possessive pronoun, then a second accent occurs on the ultima.
Example

ο γείτονάς μας [o ˈʝi.to.'nas mas] ("our neighbor")

φύλαξέ το [ˈfi.laks.'e to] ("keep it")

απέναντí μας [a.'pe.nand.'i mas] ("opposite us")

  • If an imperative verb has a paroxytone accent and is followed by two weak personal pronouns, then the one closest to it also has an accent.
Example

δώσε τού το ['ðo.se 'tu to] ("give it to him")

φέρε μού τα [ˈfe.re 'mu ta] ("bring them to me")

This secondary stress is also marked by an acute accent.

docs.title: Personal Pronouns
docs.text:
First-Person Personal Pronouns Singular Plural Strong Weak Strong Weak Nominative εγώ - εμείς - Genitive εμένα μου εμάς μας Accusative εμένα με εμάς μας

When used with the [[Prepositions|prepositions]] "για" and "από", the pronoun "εμένα" loses the initial "ε", i.e. "για μένα" and "από μένα" instead of "για εμένα" and "από εμένα".

Second-Person Personal Pronouns Singular Plural Strong Weak Strong Weak Nominative εσύ - εσείς - Genitive εσένα σου εσάς σας Accusative εσένα σε εσάς σας Vocative εσύ - εσείς -

When used with the [[Prepositions|prepositions]] "για" and "από", the pronoun "εσένα" loses the initial "ε", i.e. "για σένα" and "από σένα" instead of "για εσένα" and "από εσένα".

Third Person Personal Pronouns Singular Plural Masculine Feminine Neuter Masculine Feminine Neuter Nominative αυτός αυτή αυτό αυτοί αυτές αυτά Genitive αυτού, του αυτής, της αυτού, του αυτών, τους Nominative αυτόν,τον αυτή(ν), τη(ν) αυτό, το αυτούς, τους αυτές, τις, τες αυτά, τα

The third person accusative of the feminine singular ends in -ν when the following word starts with a vowel or κ, π, τ, ξ, ψ, γκ, μπ, ντ. In all other situations, the -ν is optional.

Note: Pronoun Ambiguity

Sometimes, there may be ambiguity about whether a pronoun in a sentence is genitive personal pronoun or a [[Pronouns#Possessive Pronouns|possessive pronoun]]. This is resolved in speech by placing stress on the pronoun and in writing by adding and accent mark on it if it is a [[Pronouns#Personal Pronoun|personal pronoun]]. However, there is no need for an accent mark in writing when both a [[Pronouns#Personal Pronouns|personal pronoun]] and a [[Pronouns#Possessive Pronouns|possessive pronoun]] are used, since it is obvious which is which in this case.

Example: Ambiguous Pronouns

Ο καθηγητής μού εξήγησε το μάθημα. - The teacher explained the lesson to me.

Ο καθηγητής μου εξήγησε το μάθημα. - My teacher explained the lesson.

Ο καθηγητής μου μου εξήγησε το μάθημα. - My teacher explained the lesson to me.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The nominative personal pronouns are not necessary because the verb conjugation shows who the subject is. Instead, these pronouns are usually used for emphasis in order to show that a specific someone and not someone else is doing the action.

Personal pronouns which only have one form can also be used either before or after the verb. Wherever there are two forms separated by a comma, the longer form is known as the strong form of the personal pronoun and the shorter is its weak form. This distinction is very important because the different forms can only take specific places in the sentence: - Strong forms can come either before or after the verb. - Weak forms always precede the verb in indicative and subjunctive sentences. The only exception is "τες" which always follows the verb. - Weak forms, however, always follow verbs in the imperative mood and participles.

Example: Position of the Personal Pronouns

Εγώ θα πληρώσω. / Θα πληρώσω εγώ. (I will pay.)

Τον βλέπω. / Αυτόν βλέπω. / Βλέπω αυτόν. (I see him.)

Τη βλέπω. / Αυτή βλέπω. / Βλέπω αυτή. (I see her.)

Αν τις δεις, φώναξέ τες. (If you see them, call them.)

Δώσε μου το μολύβι. (Give me the pencil.)

Τραγουδούσε κοιτάζοντάς τη στα μάτια. (Looking her in the eyes, he was singing.)

It is also quite common to see the strong and the weak form of the same personal pronoun used one after ther other.

Example

Εμένα με λένε Ελένη. (They call me Helen.)

docs.title: Possessive Pronouns
docs.text:
Possesive pronouns in modern Greek are fairly simple because they do not change depending on the case. Moreover, the forms of the possessive pronouns are exactly the same as the [[Pronouns#Personal Pronouns|weak forms]] of the genitive [[Pronouns#Personal Pronouns|personal pronouns]].

Singular Plural 1st Person μου μας 2nd Person σου σας 3rd Person(Masculine) του τους 3rd Person(Feminine) της τους 3rd Person(Neuter) του τους

Note

Masculine / feminine / neuter refers to the owner and not the thing owned.

Possessive pronouns are always used in conjunction with an [[Articles|article]] and come directly after the thing which is being "owned". Additionally, they are never stressed.

Example: Basic Usage of Possessive Pronouns

η τσάντα μου (my bag) - Η τσάντα μου είναι ροζ. (My bag is pink.)

το τηλέφωνό σου (your phone) - Μου αρέσει το χρώμα τou τηλέφωνού σου. (I like the color of your phone.)

ο σκύλος του (his dog) - Ο σκύλος του είναι πολύ φιλικός. (His dog is very friendly.)

η γάτα της (her cat) - Η γάτα της κοιμάται. (Her cat is sleeping).

η πόρτα του (its door) - Η πόρτα του είναι παλιά. (Its door is old. For example, the house's door.)

το σπίτι μας (our house) - Το σπίτι μας είναι μεγάλο. (Our house is big.)

ο φίλος σας (your friend) - Βλέπω τον φίλο σας. (I see your friend).

το βιβλίο τους (their book) - Θέλο να αγοράσω το βιβλίο τους. (I want to buy their book.)

If we want to use a possessive pronoun on its own, then we always have to use it with the [[Adjectives|adjective]] δικός, ή, ό. The adjective is declined in accordance with the noun being "owned", even though the noun itself is not present in the sentence. This usage is usually equivalent to the English mine, yours, hers, ours, etc.

Example: Standalone Possessive Pronouns

Αυτό το βιβλίο είναι δικό μου. (This book is mine.)

The [[Adjectives|adjective]] δικός, ή, ό can also be used to emphasise that the thing being possessed belongs to a particular owner and not to someone or something else. In this case, however, the adjective and the possessive pronoun are placed directly after the [[Articles|definite article]]. In this usage, the phrasing may also be similar to the English "my / your / his / hers / its / our / your / their own".

Emphasising Possessive Pronouns

Γιατί φοράς συνέχεια τις δικές μου κάλτσες? - Why are you wearing my socks? (and not yours)

Μένουν στο δικό τους σπίτι. - They live in their own house.

docs.title: Relative Pronouns
docs.text:
Relative pronouns are used to introduce relative clauses.

The most common relative pronoun is που. It is indeclinable and can stand for any noun regardless of its gender, case or number.

Example: The Relative Pronoun "που"

Έχασα το βιβλίο που μου δάνεισες. (I lost the book which you gave me.)

The relative pronoun οποίος, οποία, οποίο is a more formal equivalent of που. It is always preceded by the [[Articles|definite article]] and must agree in gender, case and number with the noun it refers to. It is declined like an [[Adjectives|adjective]] ending in -ος, -α, -ο.

Example: οποίος, οποία, οποίο

Έχασα το βιβλίο το οποίο μου δάνεισες. (I lost the book which you gave me.)

The relative pronoun όποιος, όποια, όποιο means "whoever" / "whichever" / "anyone who". It is used without the [[Articles|definite article]] and declines like an [[Adjectives|adjective]] ending in -ος, -α, -ο.

Example: όποιος, όποια, όποιο

Όπιος θέλει μπορεί να έρθει μαζί μας. (Whoever wants can come with us.)

The construction "ό, τι" serves a very similar purpose as όποιος, όποια, όποιο but can only be used with inanimate objects and is indeclinable. It is best translated as "whatever" / "what" / "any".

Example: ό, τι

Θα φάω ό, τι βρω στο ψυγείο. (I will eat whatever I find in the fridge.)

The relative pronoun όσος, όση, όσο means "as much as" / "as many as". It is used without the [[Articles|definite article]] and must agree in gender, case and number with the noun it refers to. It declines like an [[Adjectives|adjective]] ending in -ος, -η, -ο.

Example: όσος, όση, όσο

Θα αγοράσω όσα μήλα θέλεις. (I will buy as many apples as you want.)

docs.title: Demonstrative Pronouns
docs.text:
Demonstrative pronouns indicate which specific object a person is talking about.

The pronoun αυτός, αυτή, αυτό can be translated as "this" / "these" and is used whenever the object is close to the speaker. It must agree in gender, case and number with the [[Nouns|noun]] it refers to and declines like an [[Adjectives|adjective]] ending in -ος, -η, -ο. This pronoun is always used in conjunction with the [[Articles|definite]] article and is placed right before it.

Example: αυτός, αυτή, αυτό

Μπράβο σου για αυτό το ρόλο. (Congratulations for this role.)

The pronoun εκείνος, εκείνη, εκείνο can be translated as "that" / "those" and is used whenever the object is farther from the speaker. It must agree in gender, case and number with the [[Nouns|noun]] it refers to and declines like an [[Adjectives|adjective]] ending in -ος, -η, -ο. This pronoun is always used in conjunction with the [[Articles|definite]] article and is placed right before it.

Example: εκείνος, εκείνη, εκείνο

Εκείνο το βιβλίο είναι δικό μου. (That book is mine.)

docs.title: Interrogative Pronouns
docs.text:
The interrogative pronoun "τι" is used to ask questions about inanimate objects and is indeclinable.

Example: Questions with τι

Τι κάνεις? (What are you doing?)

Με τι γράφεις? (What are you writing with?)

Από τι ώρα περιμένεις? (Since what time are you waiting?)

The interrogative pronoun ποιος, ποια, ποιο is used for asking questions about people and for asking questions about inanimate objects when there is a limited number of them and the speaker essentially wants to "choose" one over the others. The pronoun must agree with the thing it refers to in gender, case and number. It is declined like an [[Adjectives|adjective]] ending in -ος, -α, -ο, although the genetive singular and genitive plural can also have the forms ποιανού and ποιανών, respectively.

Example: Questions with ποιος, ποια, ποιο

Ποιος είναι αυτός? - Who is this? (asking about a man)

Ποια είναι αυτή? - Who is this? (asking about a woman)

Ποια ταινία θέλεις να δούμε? - Which movie do you want to watch?

Ποιο χρώμα προτιμάς? - Which color do you prefer?

The interrogative pronouns τίνος and τίνων are used to enquire about the owner of something. The former is used when the thing is singular and the latter is used when the thing is plural.

Example: Questions with τίνος / τίνων

Τίνος είναι αυτό το παλτό? - Whose coat is this?

Τίνων είναι αυτά τα παιδιά που παίζουν στην αυλή? - Whose children are these which are playing in the yard?

The interrogative pronoun πόσος, πόση, πόσο is used for asking about quantity and can be translated as "how much" / "how many". It is declined like an [[Adjectives|adjective]] ending in -ος, -η, -ο and must agree with the thing it refers to in gender, case and number.

Example: Questions with πόσος, πόση, πόσο

Πόσο γάλα θέλεις στον καφέ σου? - How much milk do you want in your coffee?

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: The most common word order in modern Greek is Subject-Verb-Object but the language's rich inflectional system allows for many variations which also appear frequently.

docs.title: Case System
docs.text:
Modern Greek has a case system to show the role which each noun plays in the sentence. This role is reflected by a change in the noun's form.

There are four cases in modern Greek - nominative, genitive, accusative and vocative.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text:
Verbs in [[./index|Modern Greek]] can be either in the active voice or the mediopassive voice. The voice is indicated by a verb's stem and the ending it takes.

In general, the two voices are used as follows: - The active voice indicates that the action is being done by the subject of the sentence; - The medio-passive voice indicates that the action is being done to the subject of the sentence.

However, certain verbs, known as deponent verbs, always use the passive-voice endings but have an active meaning when translated in English.

docs.title: Aspect
docs.text:
The [[TODO|aspect]] (ποιόν ενεργείας) of a [[Verbs#Verbs|verb]] shows how the action is perceived by the speaker. Every [[Verbs|verb]] in [[./index|Modern Greek]] is in one of three [[TODO|aspects]]: - The imperfective aspect (ατελές) represent actions which are perceived to be in progress, habitual or repeated. - The perfective aspect (τέλειο) represents actions which are perceived as a completed whole or in a neutral way, without reference to duration or frequency; - The perfect aspect (συντελεσμένο) also represents actions which are perceived as a completed whole but puts more emphasis on the result of those actions rather than the actions themselves.

Whether a [[Verbs|verb]] is [[Verbs#Aspect|imperfective]] or [[Verbs#Aspect|perfective]] is marked by its stem. The [[Verbs#Aspect|perfect aspect]] is formed by adding the suffix -ει to a [[Verbs#Aspect|perfective stem]]. The forms of the [[Verbs#Aspect|perfect aspect]] are also known as nonfinite forms because they are only used in specific constructions and do not change by adding endings.

Example: Aspect

Verb Imperfective Perfective Perfect Active Passive Active Passive Active Passive γράφω ("to write") γραφ- γραψ- γραφ-, γραφτ- γραψει γραφεί, γραφτεί εμπνέω ("to inspire") εμπνε- εμπνευσ- εμπνευστ-, εμπνευσθ- εμπνεύσει εμπνευστεί, εμπνευσθεί

The vast majority of [[Verbs|verbs]] have forms for both the [[Verbs#Aspect|imperfective]] and the [[Verbs#Aspect|perfective]], but some exist in only one or the other. As such, if a [[Verbs|verb]] does not exist in the [[Verbs#Aspect|perfective]], then it also cannot exist in the [[Verbs#Aspect|perfect]].

Many [[Verbs|verbs]] can be categorized depending on the patterns followed by their [[Verbs#Aspect|imperfective]] and the [[Verbs#Aspect|perfective]] stems.
